title: Technology Sector Update for 11/02/2018: BABA,VRSN,ANET,AAPL

Technology stocks continued to fall in afternoon trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 dropping just over 2.0% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was posting a nearly 1.5% decrease.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Alibaba Group Holding ( BABA ) was almost 2% lower this afternoon, drifting off a slightly more than 2% gain for the Chinese internet conglomerate after it reported Q2 net income exceeding Wall Street forecasts. The company earned RMB9.60, or $1.40, per share, improving on an RMB8.57 profit during the same quarter last year and topping the Capital IQ consensus expecting $1.11 per share. Revenue jumped 54% year over year to $12.4 billion but missed the $12.5 billion analyst mean. Alibaba also raised its FY19 revenue outlook by 4% to 6% over its previous guidance, now expecting between RMB375 billion to RMB383 billion, with revenue growth seen reaching 60% by the January-to-March quarter.
In other sector news:
(+) VeriSign ( VRSN ) soared to its best share price since the height of the internet boom in September 2000, rising over 25% to $176.59 a share after the domain name registry company reported Q3 net income of $1.23 per share, up from $1.00 per share during the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.04 per share. Revenue increased 4.6% to $305.8 million from $292.4 million last year and nudging past the $305.48 million analyst mean.
(+) Arista Networks ( ANET ) was nearly 6% higher in recent trade, giving back almost half of a nearly 12% gain earlier in Friday's session that followed the cloud networking company reporting improved Q3 financial results and beating Wall Street expectations, prompting analysts at RBC Capital Markets to increase their price target for the company's stock by $10 to $300 a share. Excluding one-time items, net income rose to $2.11 per share from $1.62 per share last year while revenue grew 29% year-over-year to $563.3 million. Analysts, on average, had been expecting a non-GAAP profit of $1.85 per share on $548.81 million in sales.
(-) Apple ( AAPL ) slumped badly Friday, recently falling over 7%, after chief financial officer CFO Luca Maestri said during a conference call late Thursday the technology giant will no longer provide iPhone unit sales data starting with results for the current quarter ending Dec. 31. The announcement upstaged better-than-expected fiscal Q4 financial results, earning $2.91 per share on $62.90 billion in sales compared with the Street view expecting $2.78 per share on $61.6 billion in sales. iPhone sales were little changed from year-ago levels at 46.9 million compared with 46.7 million during the September quarter in 2017.
